what_this_is: Every plain-English claim the web view makes about biology, as data rather than as prose inside the renderer. The numbers on that page are generated from result files; the words were not, and the words carry claims. This file is where they are reviewable, correctable and attributable. Nothing here is measured: it is background knowledge, written by hand, and the renderer may assemble sentences from it but may not add to it.
how_to_correct_it: Edit an entry. The renderer reads this file and has no vocabulary of its own, so a wrong gloss is wrong in exactly one place. An entry whose basis cannot be stated should be deleted rather than softened.

polymerase.basis: the gene_role the committed Pfam scan assigned, from the family name RNA_replicase_B. In a positive-sense RNA virus the replicase is the enzyme that copies the genome.

coat.basis: Pfam family Levi_coat. The coat protein is the structural subunit the particle is built from.

capsid.basis: the same structural role under the name the scoring stage used for it.

maturation.basis: Pfam family Phage_mat-A. In Leviviricetes the maturation protein is the single copy incorporated into the particle that binds the host pilus and carries the genome in; it is the gene in contact with the host, which is why its divergence is reported separately.

other.basis: no role assigned. Either no Pfam domain was found or the domain carries no role in this table. It is not a claim that the gene has no function.

ssrna_phage.label: single-stranded RNA bacteriophage
ssrna_phage.expected_roles_plain: the three genes such a phage needs: one to attach to a bacterium, one to build the shell it travels in, and one to copy its genome
ssrna_phage.basis: ICTV class Leviviricetes: positive-sense single-stranded RNA bacteriophages of 3 to 4.5 kb carrying a maturation protein, a coat protein and a replicase. The three Pfam families above are that class's own families, so a contig carrying them is an RNA phage by the same evidence that named its genes.
ssrna_phage.what_this_call_is_not: it is a call about the nearest reference material, not an isolation. Nothing here has been grown, and a sequence that carries a phage's genes in a phage's arrangement is read as a phage because that is what the evidence supports, not because the organism was observed.

environmental_record.plain: an unnamed sequence from another environmental sample
environmental_record.basis: a RefSeq title of the form 'ssRNA phage SRRxxxxxxx_n' or one marked MAG names a record assembled from a metagenome and given a placeholder name, not a characterised isolate. The substring is the whole test, so a record named some other way will not be recognised and is reported as unknown rather than as characterised.

status: hand-written background knowledge. It is not a result, carries no seed and no run, and is listed in the web view's Methods as what it is.
